title: Local null-homotopy from a strictly perfect complex into an upper-acyclic complex
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a site with a sheaf of commutative rings, with module sheaves and their integer-indexed cochain complexes and cohomology [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $U$ be an object and work on the localized ringed site $(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal O_U)$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let $a\in\mathbf Z$ and let $P^\bullet,K^\bullet$ be complexes of $\mathcal O_U$-modules. Assume $P^j=0$ outside a finite interval, each $P^j$ is a direct summand of a finite free $\mathcal O_U$-module, $P^j=0$ for $j<a$, and $H^j(K^\bullet)=0$ for every $j\geq a$. For every chain map $w:P^\bullet\to K^\bullet$ there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ on which $w$ is chain homotopic to zero: there are morphisms $h_i^j:P^j|_{U_i}\to K^{j-1}|_{U_i}$ such that $w^j|_{U_i}=d_K^{j-1}h_i^j+h_i^{j+1}d_P^j$ for all $j\in\mathbf Z$. No boundedness of $K^\bullet$ is assumed.

proof.text: Work throughout on a slice $\mathcal C/V$ over $U$. Restriction to a further slice is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]; therefore it preserves kernels, images and their quotients, and $H^n(K|_V)=H^n(K)|_V=0$ for $n\geq a$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Restrictions are sectionwise and relocalize as in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]; in particular they preserve finite free modules, displayed retracts, and every equation between module maps. Thus all the hypotheses needed below persist after any covering refinement.

source.place: Tag 08FP, lemma-local-homotopy (2), finite induction on the support; Tag 08FN, lemma-local-lift-map, finite basis lifts.

proof.text: Choose $b\geq a$ with $P^j=0$ for $j>b$. We construct the homotopy in the finite descending order $b,b-1,\ldots,a$. Initially set $h^j=0$ for $j>b$, so $w^j=d_K^{j-1}h^j+h^{j+1}d_P^j$ holds for $j>b$. At stage $n$ assume these identities for $j>n$, on a current covering member $V$. Put $r^n=w^n-h^{n+1}d_P^n$. The chain-map identity and the identity already obtained in degree $n+1$ give $d_K^n r^n=(w^{n+1}-d_K^n h^{n+1})d_P^n=h^{n+2}d_P^{n+1}d_P^n=0$. Hence $r^n$ factors through $Z^n=\ker(d_K^n)$, by the defining property of a kernel [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 08FP, lemma-local-homotopy (2), finite induction on the support; Tag 08FN, lemma-local-lift-map, finite basis lifts.

proof.text: Since $n\geq a$, the quotient $Z^n/\operatorname{im}(d_K^{n-1})=H^n(K)$ is zero. Thus the differential with codomain restricted to cycles is an epimorphism $p_n:K^{n-1}\to Z^n$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Forgetting module structure preserves cokernels by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], so this is also an epimorphism of abelian sheaves. Its sheafification hypothesis holds on these sites and their slices: ordinary abelian sheafification is among the value categories of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] to conclude that every section of $Z^n$ over the terminal object of $\mathcal C/V$ lifts locally through $p_n$.

source.place: Tag 08FP, lemma-local-homotopy (2), finite induction on the support; Tag 08FN, lemma-local-lift-map, finite basis lifts.

proof.text: Choose a retraction $P^n\xrightarrow{i}\mathcal O_V^{\oplus t}\xrightarrow{q}P^n$, $qi=1$. For each of the finitely many standard generators $e_\ell$, lift the section $(r^n q)(e_\ell)$ of $Z^n$ using Step 3. Successively refine these covers; the covering pullback and composition axioms [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] give one covering of $V$ carrying all $t$ lifts. On each member their $\mathcal O$-linear extension is a module-sheaf morphism $s:\mathcal O^{\oplus t}\to K^{n-1}$: over $W$ it sends $(c_\ell)$ to $\sum c_\ell y_\ell|_W$, which commutes with restrictions [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The equality $p_ns=r^nq$ holds on each generator and therefore on every section. Set $h^n=si$; then $p_nh^n=r^nqi=r^n$, giving the homotopy identity in degree $n$. For $t=0$ take the identity cover and the zero map. Restricting the previously chosen $h^j$ leaves all higher identities intact [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

source.place: Tag 08FP, lemma-local-homotopy (2), finite induction on the support; Tag 08FN, lemma-local-lift-map, finite basis lifts.

proof.text: Repeat Steps 2--4 for the $b-a+1$ degrees. Only finitely many coverings are composed, and their composites cover $U$ by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; relocalization [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] identifies the final sheaves with $P|_{U_i}$ and $K|_{U_i}$. Set $h^j=0$ also for $j<a$. The identities in $[a,b]$ hold by construction. In every other degree $P^j=0$, so both $w^j$ and the two terms on the right are zero (in degree $a-1$ this uses $d_P^{a-1}=0$). These are exactly all the requested homotopy equations. If $P=0$ the zero homotopy on the identity cover suffices. No step requires any lower or upper bound on $K$.
